content:
Hello world!,

I am reorganizing my current project and trying to get into some kind of standard presentation that will be user-friendly to the mathlib community. I've read through a number of lean4/github documents and am left with the following confusion:

Initially I used lake init and was left with a /foo/Foo file structure that seemed redundant to me within my own use case. Is that something that should be maintained, or is it safe to change this? I would prefer to have a root directory /foo with /foo/src containing all of the source code. Is that not the normal way?

My current math is apparently most closely aligned with discrete dynamics, so I am tempted to create /foo/src/DiscreteDynamics and place my source code within. Is that (the most) correct?

In the near future, I will be adding some modules that will be largely related to combinatorics, so my thinking here was to later have /src/Combinatorics...

Edit: figured a few of these out...

Is there a preference to using a .toml or a lakefile.lean file for initiating lake? I currently have a lakefile...

Edit: I've also looked at github examples for papers using lean4 formal proofs, and I can see there isn't a real standard, so I apologize for using that term... I'm just trying to find a structure and naming convention that is going to be readily understood under the standards otherwise used for mathlib.

Thank you for your help,
Ian

Also I found this sentence in the documentation at https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Build-Tools-and-Distribution/Lake/ in section 24.1.1 Concepts and Terminology:

"The direct dependencies of a package are those that it requires, and the transitive dependencies are the direct dependencies of a package together with their transitive dependencies." My head is now going around in circles. :sob:
